questions.question: [Analysing Dance Performance] Q: What is the advantage of watching a live performance over a recorded one?
questions.correctAnswer: Live performance provides the full sensory experience — you feel the energy, scale and atmosphere in real time, and the audience-performer relationship is immediate and tangible.
questions.explanation: Live performance provides the full sensory experience — you feel the energy, scale and atmosphere in real time, and the audience-performer relationship is immediate and tangible.

questions.question: [Analysing Dance Performance] Q: Why is repeated viewing useful when analysing a recorded dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated viewing lets you focus on different elements each time — first the overall structure, then specific movement details, design features or dancer relationships.
questions.explanation: Repeated viewing lets you focus on different elements each time — first the overall structure, then specific movement details, design features or dancer relationships.

questions.question: [Analysing Dance Performance] Q: How do the four content categories help structure an analysis?
questions.correctAnswer: They provide a systematic framework so you cover all aspects: action (what), dynamics (how), space (where) and relationships (who), ensuring nothing is missed.
questions.explanation: They provide a systematic framework so you cover all aspects: action (what), dynamics (how), space (where) and relationships (who), ensuring nothing is missed.

questions.question: [Artificial Things — Lucy Bennett] Q: What is the choreographic intention of 'Artificial Things'?
questions.correctAnswer: To explore human connection and the idea of finding joy and possibility despite limitations, celebrating how collaboration creates something greater than individual constraints.
questions.explanation: To explore human connection and the idea of finding joy and possibility despite limitations, celebrating how collaboration creates something greater than individual constraints.

questions.question: [Artificial Things — Lucy Bennett] Q: Why is Stopgap Dance Company significant in the context of this work?
questions.correctAnswer: Stopgap is an integrated company of disabled and non-disabled dancers — the work's meaning depends on this inclusive casting, as the dancers' different bodies directly embody the theme of overcoming limitations.
questions.explanation: Stopgap is an integrated company of disabled and non-disabled dancers — the work's meaning depends on this inclusive casting, as the dancers' different bodies directly embody the theme of overcoming limitations.

questions.question: [Artificial Things — Lucy Bennett] Q: How does David Toole contribute to the work?
questions.correctAnswer: David Toole is a disabled dancer whose powerful upper-body movement, floor work and expressive quality are central to the work — his performance embodies the theme of transcending physical limitations.
questions.explanation: David Toole is a disabled dancer whose powerful upper-body movement, floor work and expressive quality are central to the work — his performance embodies the theme of transcending physical limitations.

questions.question: [Choreographic Devices] Q: What is the difference between unison and canon?
questions.correctAnswer: In unison, all dancers move at the same time; in canon, dancers start the same phrase at different times in sequence.
questions.explanation: In unison, all dancers move at the same time; in canon, dancers start the same phrase at different times in sequence.

questions.question: [Choreographic Devices] Q: Describe how accumulation works as a choreographic device.
questions.correctAnswer: Accumulation starts with one movement, then adds a second so both are performed, then a third, and so on — the phrase gradually grows longer with each repetition.
questions.explanation: Accumulation starts with one movement, then adds a second so both are performed, then a third, and so on — the phrase gradually grows longer with each repetition.

questions.question: [Choreographic Devices] Q: Why might a choreographer use retrograde in a dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Retrograde creates a striking visual effect, like rewinding time. It can symbolise memory, returning to the past, or give a phrase a surprising twist that maintains audience interest.
questions.explanation: Retrograde creates a striking visual effect, like rewinding time. It can symbolise memory, returning to the past, or give a phrase a surprising twist that maintains audience interest.

questions.question: [Choreographic Intention & Communication] Q: What is choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Choreographic intention is the purpose or message the choreographer wants to communicate through the dance — it guides every creative decision.
questions.explanation: Choreographic intention is the purpose or message the choreographer wants to communicate through the dance — it guides every creative decision.

questions.question: [Choreographic Intention & Communication] Q: How do motifs help communicate choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Motifs are key movement phrases that embody the core idea. By developing and varying motifs throughout the dance, the choreographer reinforces the intention so the audience recognises and understands it.
questions.explanation: Motifs are key movement phrases that embody the core idea. By developing and varying motifs throughout the dance, the choreographer reinforces the intention so the audience recognises and understands it.

questions.question: [Choreographic Intention & Communication] Q: Why might an audience interpret a dance differently from the choreographer's intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Each audience member brings their own experiences and perspectives, so they may understand the movement in a different way. Multiple interpretations are valid and enrich the dance.
questions.explanation: Each audience member brings their own experiences and perspectives, so they may understand the movement in a different way. Multiple interpretations are valid and enrich the dance.
